The engraved title of the plate. "Śrī" is both an honorific and a name of Lakṣmī / Tripurasundarī; "yantram" means instrument or device — a geometric support for meditation and worship.

content.iast: oṁ śrīṁ hrīṁ śrīṁ kamale kamalālaye prasīda prasīda śrīṁ hrīṁ śrīṁ mahālakṣmyai namaḥ

translation.en: Oṁ. Śrīṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ. O Kamalā, dweller in the lotus, be gracious, be gracious. Śrīṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ. Salutations to Mahālakṣmī.

explanation.en: The Mahālakṣmī mantra, engraved as the closing dedication of the plate. It is built around the bīja (seed) syllables śrīṁ (Lakṣmī) and hrīṁ (Bhuvaneśvarī / the creative māyā-śakti), addressed to the goddess as Kamalā, "she of the lotus." Traditionally recited for abundance and grace.

tārā-nāyaka-śekharāṁ smita-mukhīm āpīna-vakṣoruhām ।

translation.en: Her form red as vermilion, three-eyed, her ruby diadem gleaming, crested with the moon — lord of the stars — her face smiling, her bosom full…

explanation.en: The first half of the classic dhyāna-śloka (visualization verse) of Tripurasundarī, the deity of the Śrī Yantra. The verse continues in the bottom-right corner of the plate. Reciting it, the practitioner builds the goddess's image in the mind before worship of the yantra.

translation.en: …holding in her two hands a jeweled cup brimming with nectar and a red lotus, gentle, her red feet resting upon a pot of jewels — thus should one meditate on the supreme Mother.

explanation.en: The second half of the Tripurasundarī dhyāna-śloka begun in the bottom-left corner. Together the two halves form one verse: the complete mental image of the goddess to be held while contemplating the yantra.

The ninth and innermost āvaraṇa, the Sarvānanda-maya cakra — "formed of all bliss." The bindu is the seat of Mahātripurasundarī herself, the undivided source from which the nine interlocking triangles and all outer enclosures emanate. In śrī-vidyā practice the eye is led inward through the āvaraṇas to rest here. On this plate the bīja syllables klīṁ and sauḥ are engraved beside the bindu.

North-east corner (top-left): the siddhi **prākāmya** — 'irresistible will — obtaining whatever one wishes' — preceded by its bīja *prāṁ*.

The **siddhis** (सिद्धि, attainments — the yogic powers) are the deities of the bhūpura's outermost line. This plate places one at each gate (aṇimā west, laghimā north, mahimā east, īśitva south) and one in each corner (vaśitva NW, prākāmya NE, bhukti SE, icchā SW), each written with a bīja made from its first syllable plus anusvāra. East is at the top of the plate.

**Īśānī** is the direction of Īśāna (Śiva as regent of the north-east). The four gates are labelled with the cardinal directions. On this plate **east (पूर्वा) is at the top**, south (दक्षिणा) on the right, west (पश्चिमा) at the bottom and north (उत्तरा) on the left; the corners carry the intermediate directions (ईशानी NE, आग्नेयी SE, नैर्ऋति SW, वायवी NW). The feminine forms (pūrvā, dakṣiṇā…) agree with *diś*, 'direction'.

translation.en: the powers of the bow and of the noose

explanation.en: Engraved just above the central triangle: **dhanuḥ-śakti**, the power of the bow, and **pāśa-śakti**, the power of the noose. Kāmeśvara and Kāmeśvarī hold four weapons — the sugar-cane bow, the five flower arrows, the noose and the goad — and these are worshipped as goddesses around the central triangle before its three corner goddesses. The arrow mantra of the same set is engraved in the block at the bottom-left of the square.

content.iast: kaṁ khaṁ gaṁ ghaṁ ṅaṁ anaṅga-kusumā

translation.en: ka-group letters; Kusumā — flower of the Bodiless One

explanation.en:

translation.en: ṝṁ — gandhākarṣiṇī, she who attracts smell (gandha)

content.iast:
bindu trikoṇa catuṣkoṇa daśārayugma
manvastra nāgadala ṣoḍaśa patrayuktam |
vṛtatrayaṁ ca dharaṇīsadanatrayaṁ
ca śrī cakram etad uditaṁ
paradevatāyāḥ ||

translation.en: Point, triangle, eight-triangle figure, two ten-triangle figures, fourteen-triangle figure, 8- and 16-petalled lotuses, three circles and the three-line earth-house: this is the Śrī Cakra of the Supreme Goddess.

explanation.en:
The classical definition of the Śrī Cakra, engraved twice on this plate (here and in the opposite corner):

*bindu-trikoṇa-catuṣkoṇa-daśārayugma-manvasra-nāgadala-ṣoḍaśa-patrayuktam | vṛttatrayaṁ ca dharaṇīsadanatrayaṁ ca śrīcakram etad uditaṁ paradevatāyāḥ ||*

"Point, triangle, the eight-cornered figure (the plate writes *catuṣkoṇa*, 'four-cornered', where the received text has *vasukoṇa*), the pair of ten-triangle figures, the fourteen-triangle figure (*manu* = 14), the eight-petalled (*nāga* = 8) and sixteen-petalled lotuses, the three circles and the three lines of the earth-house — this is declared the Śrī Cakra of the Supreme Goddess."

It lists the nine āvaraṇas from the centre outward and is the verse by which the diagram is checked.

uparī dhārāti rahasya yoginye namaḥ
tripurāyai tripureśyaya tripura sundarī
tripuravāsinyai tripuraśriya

translation.en: The ninth āvaraṇa, the Sarvānandamaya cakra; salutation to the (Parāparāti-)rahasya yoginī; to Tripurā, Tripureśī, Tripurasundarī, Tripuravāsinī, Tripurāśrī.

explanation.en: A note on the centre and its goddesses. Line 1 names the **ninth āvaraṇa**, the bindu, *Sarvānandamaya cakra* ('made of all bliss'). translation.en: …drāṁ hrīṁ klīṁ blūṁ saḥ — salutation to the arrows of Kāmeśvarī and Kāmeśvara; 5 Mahākāmeśvarī, 6 Mahāvajreśvarī, 7 Mahābhagamālinī, 8 Śrī…

explanation.en: A worn and partly garbled block belonging to the **eighth āvaraṇa**, the central triangle. The first lines are the mantra of the five flower-arrows of Kāmeśvara and Kāmeśvarī — the seed syllables normally read *drāṁ drīṁ klīṁ blūṁ saḥ* (here द्रा ही क्ली खू स) — ending *kāmeśvarī-kāmeśvara-bāṇebhyo namaḥ*, 'salutation to the arrows of Kāmeśvarī and Kāmeśvara' (the plate writes वाण for बाण). The numbered names that follow are the three goddesses of the triangle's corners, **Mahākāmeśvarī (5), Mahāvajreśvarī (6), Mahābhagamālinī (7)**, and **8 Śrī…**, presumably Śrī (Mahā)tripurasundarī at the bindu. The numbers 1–4 are evidently the four weapons (arrows, bow, noose, goad) whose bīja-line opens the block.

A single downward-pointing triangle engraved in the empty field of the bhūpura. The inverted triangle is the yoni, the emblem of Śakti — the same form as the central trikoṇa of the yantra — and is sometimes drawn on a plate as a maker's or consecration mark.

A running band of **svastikas** frames the whole plate. The svastika (स्वस्तिक, from *su-asti*, 'well-being') is the oldest Indian sign of auspiciousness and protection; on yantras, doorways and ritual vessels it wards the enclosure and invokes good fortune. Here it plays the role of an outermost, purely decorative rampart around the bhūpura.

content.devanagari: चं छं जं झं ञं अनंग मेखला
content.iast: caṁ chaṁ jaṁ jhaṁ ñaṁ anaṅga-mekhalā

translation.en: ca-group letters; Mekhalā — girdle of the Bodiless One

explanation.en:
Petal 2 of the **eight-petalled lotus — āvaraṇa 3, the Sarvasaṁkṣobhaṇa cakra** ('the wheel that agitates all'). Its eight goddesses are the powers of **Anaṅga**, 'the Bodiless One' — Kāma, the god of love, burnt to bodilessness by Śiva's glance: here anaṅga-mekhalā, 'girdle of the Bodiless One'. Each petal also carries one group of the consonants (caṁ chaṁ jaṁ jhaṁ ñaṁ), continuing the alphabet whose vowels stand on the sixteen petals outside; the letters are engraved first, the name after them.

The goddesses of this ring are the *guptatara-yoginīs* ('more hidden yoginīs'); its presiding goddess is Tripurasundarī and its mudrā Sarvākarṣiṇī. The plate places the first four goddesses at the cardinal points (1 east = top, 2 south = right, 3 west = bottom, 4 north = left) and the last four in the corners between them, the classical order of worship.

Triangle 10 of 10 in the **inner ten-triangle ring — āvaraṇa 6, the Sarvarakṣākara cakra** ('protector of all'). Its goddess is **Sarvepsitaphalapradā**, 'giver of every wished-for fruit'.

The goddesses of this ring are the *nigarbha-yoginīs (yoginīs of the womb within)*; its presiding goddess is Tripuramālinī and its mudrā Sarva-mahāṅkuśā. Numbered from the bottom (west) anticlockwise. In this ring the plate switches to vowels for the letters (अं for the first, ऊं for the sixth) and writes only number, letter and cakra mark — the triangles are too small for the names.

*Reading note:* the engraving in the triangles is small and worn in places. Where the plate is legible its text is given; otherwise the name is the canonical one for this position, and the engraved letter and numeral are left out rather than guessed.

A single syllable engraved in one of the diamond-shaped gaps between the triangles. As on the square and the two lotuses, each ring of triangles carries the name of its āvaraṇa as a caption broken into syllables — चतुर्थावरणं श्रीसर्वसौभाग्यदायकचक्रं for the fourteen, पञ्चमावरणं श्रीसर्वार्थसाधकचक्रं for the outer ten, षष्ठावरणं श्रीसर्वरक्षाकरचक्रं for the inner ten, सप्तमावरणं श्रीसर्वरोगहरचक्रं for the eight — scattered through the gaps and read clockwise from the bindu. Clearly legible pieces include श्री, सर्व, सौ·भा·ग्य·दा·य·क, रक्षा and क्रं; several others are worn.
